mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds in a restrictive policy phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of months with FEDFUNDS up >0.25%, or the change in FEDFUNDS is not statistically significant with respect to SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting stronger labor market absorption and investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of zero change in PAYEMS (p > 0.05), or employment growth is below 50,000 in all months during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds its prior month by 2% or more, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, signaling resilient supply-side momentum.
regime_hint: Surprise acceleration in supply chain activity
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive months of positive INDPRO surprise, 20-day forward returns are not statistically above zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% for three consecutive months triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations of slower demand growth materialize.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in all months meeting the disinflation trigger (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of falling unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% create a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive when UNRATE stays below 4% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (HOUST) by 10% or more in a month leads to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting strong consumer demand momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average during similar sales spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and unemployment (UNRATE) by at least 1% each month creates a statistically significant positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual momentum in supply and labor.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO ↓ ≥1% AND UNRATE ↓ ≥1% in the same month
regime_hint: Concomitant declines in supply and labor frictions
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in any 12-month window with the trigger met.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis expansion phase (as indicated by a 6-month rising trend in FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting investor confidence in economic recovery.
failure_condition: In regimes satisfying the FEDFUNDS trend trigger, 20-day forward returns are not consistently positive (p > 0.05 over 5 such regimes).
